text:
maya: Quick FYI — noticed a recurring 15-40ms p50 spike on H100 when sequence length crosses ~1200 in canary (hosted). Looks like kernel routing flips between Triton path and our CUTLASS fallback.
aj: Hmm. Is this the autotuner choosing triton by default then failing at runtime? Any logs?
maya: Logs show: `chosen_kernel=triton_fast_attn`, then ~20ms later `kernel_fallback_detected=unsupported_tile_shape -> falling_back=cutlass`. Stack snippet:
```
[2026-02-14T13:02:11Z] chosen_kernel=triton_fast_attn (seqlen=1152, bsz=1)
[2026-02-14T13:02:11Z] runtime_check: unsupported_tile_shape (head_dim=128) -> fallback
[2026-02-14T13:02:11Z] route_to: cutlass_mha
```
maya: The weird part is we sometimes get triton for 1152 and sometimes cutlass — non-deterministic under identical inputs.
sasha: Could be nondeterministic kernel availability due to memory fragmentation or different kernel cache priming. Are we hitting different workspace or smem limits across calls?
ryan: Also check prefix KV cache behavior — if KV cache is warm vs cold the token distribution changes and the runtime may pick different batch sizes which affects tile packing.
aj: I ran a tiny repro on a stripped model. Observed same flip when kv_cache_enabled toggled. Warm KV -> bigger cached kv blocks -> Triton path fails tile check.
perf-bot: perf snapshot attached: p50 before flip=22ms, after flip=46ms, p90 ~120ms during fallback storms. (snapshot id: ps_20260214_001)
maya: Autotuner profile for this model suggests triton wins for seqlen<=1024 but uncertain 1024-1536. Our current decision boundary is 1150 in config.
sasha: That boundary is risky; it should be sequence-length *and* head_dim aware. H100 keeps certain tilings; A100 differs. Are we honoring architecture tag in profiles?
aj: We do store arch info but the lookup logic prefers earlier successful kernel even if hardware changed pockets. Maybe hysteresis isn't strong enough — we flip back and forth with a single failure.
ryan: Proposed: add a short cooldown on switching kernels after an unexpected fallback and require N consecutive successes before switching back. Also log SMEM/alloc failures.
maya: Agree. Also add a deterministic check: pre-validate tile shapes by running a cheap checker at kernel selection time (no launch) to avoid mid-execute fallback.
perf-bot: Simulation of hysteresis + precheck reduces flip events by 92% in a small run (n=5000 requests). p50 stable at 23ms.
infra-bot: Watchouts: precheck cost ~0.2ms per decision. In high-throughput batching this could add up; we can gate precheck to cold routes or seqlen band edges.
aj: Implementation plan: (1) add tile-shape validator in router (opt-in), (2) hysteresis state machine per model+arch+seqlen bucket with cooldown=30s and min_successes=3, (3) extra debug traces for SMEM/alloc rejections. I'll draft a PR.
sasha: Also add a telemetry metric: kernel_switch_count and fallback_reason tags (tile_shape|smem|compatibility). That will help us correlate with KV/cache warmness.
ryan: For canary: enable precheck only on canary group and adaptive hysteresis with cooldown=60s. Roll back quickly on regressions.
maya: Thanks — pushing a canary config now. Will report back in ~2 hours with traces.
aj: Thanks all. If you see runaway fallback events, @ryan please trigger a dedicated capacity fallback to keep SLAs.
maya: Update (2h later): canary looks good — flip count down to 1 in 2h vs ~37 previously. p90 improved ~30%. Leaving canary enabled for one more day.
sasha: Great. Follow-up: let's add architecture-aware default boundaries in autotuner offline job so we don't rely solely on canaries.
ryan: I'll add a ticket for autoscaling + kernel-guard integration.
maya: cc @perf-bot for daily digests of kernel_switch_count. :thumbsup:
